a5px: Read Raster Data as A5 Cells via Pixel-Driven Aggregation

Source: R/a5px-package.R
a5px-package.Rd

a5px aggregates raster pixels into A5 cells. A5 is a discrete global grid system that divides the globe into equal-area pentagonal cells at 31 resolutions. a5px streams GeoTIFF and Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF files from local disk or cloud object stores and computes per-cell statistics in a single pass, in Rust. Results are keyed by a5R cells and come back as a tibble, an Arrow table or a Parquet file.

"px" reflects the direction of the default algorithm: pixels in, cells out. Each pixel goes to the cell containing its centre, which suits cells larger than pixels. For cells smaller than pixels, mode = "centroid" samples the raster at each cell centre instead.

Reading rasters

  • a5_read_raster(): a tibble keyed by a5R::a5_cell.

  • a5_read_raster_arrow(): the same engine, returning an arrow::Table with a FixedSizeList<float, n_bands> value column.

  • a5_raster_to_parquet(): reads and writes Parquet entirely in Rust, without the R-side Arrow round trip; best for large embedding rasters.

as_vector = FALSE (default) returns one column per band; as_vector = TRUE returns one fixed-length list column per stat.

Sampling modes

  • "forward" (default): each pixel goes wholly to the cell containing its centre.

  • "overlay": each pixel is shared between the cells it overlaps, in proportion to area, so sum conserves totals.

  • "centroid": one value per cell, sampled at its centre with the interp kernel; for cells smaller than pixels.

Several files

src takes several files, read in one pass with a shared fetch queue and worker pool. separate = TRUE makes each file's bands columns, for bands stored one per file. Otherwise the files are pieces of one raster with the same bands and pixel size: every valid pixel enters its cell once, so cells on a seam combine exactly, and where files overlap every capture counts. composite instead computes stat per file and reduces across files per cell, weighted by each file's valid pixel count.

Aggregating to coarser cells

a5_aggregate() summarises an existing a5_cell-keyed result at a coarser resolution without re-reading the raster. Each cell goes to the coarse cell that contains its centre (a5R::a5_cell_to_supercell()). It handles both the wide and the list-column layout, with the same stat vocabulary as the readers.

Writing

a5px_write_parquet() writes a tibble or Arrow table from the readers to Parquet, with a schema for A5 cells and value lists.

Inspecting sources

  • a5_raster_info(): dimensions, data type, block grid, overview levels, CRS, band scale and offset, and the WGS 84 envelope, without reading pixels.

  • a5px_store_config(): the object store configuration a remote src resolves to.

Areas of interest

aoi restricts a read to the A5 cells selected from a polygon by a5R::a5_polygon_to_cells(): containment = "centre" keeps cells whose centre is inside, "overlapping" every cell the polygon touches. Selection is by cell: an included cell gets the statistics of all its valid pixels, including any outside the polygon. Tools such as exactextract instead clip pixels to the polygon; for that, aggregate the cells afterwards with coverage fractions of your choice.

Chunked reads

The accumulators hold every touched cell in memory (about 4.5 GB per million cells with 64 bands and stat = c("mean", "count")), so split very large reads by bbox. A pixel centred on an edge two chunks share belongs to one of them, so with stat = c("sum", "count") the per-cell partials of adjacent chunks add up exactly, and means follow. A remote block that several chunks touch is fetched once and then served from the session cache (a5px_set_cache()), as long as the cache holds it. With bbox_align = "block" each chunk takes whole COG blocks instead, so no chunk reads a block another chunk owns. a5_raster_info() reports the block grid and envelope to build the chunks from.

Configuration

a5px_set_concurrency() and a5px_get_concurrency() set the session defaults for the worker pool (cpu_workers) and the number of remote requests in flight (io_concurrency). They are independent of a5R::a5_set_threads(). Remote reads are usually limited by latency, so a higher io_concurrency often helps. Remote reads keep the byte ranges they fetch in a session cache, so reads split into bbox chunks fetch each block once; a5px_set_cache() sets its budget.

Common arguments

All readers accept the same core arguments:

  • src: one or more paths or URLs: local, file://, http(s)://, s3://, gs:// or az://. Remote reads fetch byte ranges and never download the whole file; see "Remote sources".

  • resolution: A5 resolution, 0 to 29 (30 is not yet supported); a5R::a5_cell_area() gives the cell area at each.

  • stat: one or more of "mean", "sum", "count", "min", "max", "var", "sd", "majority", "fractions" and "npix". Several give one column per band and stat. var and sd use the sample formula (divisor n - 1), so a cell with one pixel returns NA.

  • bands: NULL (all), 1-based indices, or names matched against the GDAL DESCRIPTION band tag. For band-interleaved files only the selected bands are fetched.

  • scoff, dequant: decode stored values per pixel before aggregation.

  • cpu_workers, io_concurrency: see a5px_set_concurrency().

Remote sources

src may be an s3://, gs://, az:// or http(s):// URL; reads are byte-range requests and the file is never downloaded whole. Cloud clients are configured from the environment first and from the readers' store_opts argument second, so an explicit option always wins. a5px_store_config() shows the resolved configuration without making a request.

  • S3: every AWS_* variable object_store understands, including AWS_REGION / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, AWS_ENDPOINT / AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI and AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE, plus GDAL's AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST=YES for public buckets (mapped to aws_skip_signature). Without static, container or web-identity credentials the client takes them from the instance metadata service (on EC2, ECS or Batch); where none answers within 300 ms and signing was not set either way, requests go unsigned, which reads public data and gets "access denied" from a private bucket. The shared credentials file (~/.aws/credentials) and AWS_PROFILE are not read. With no region the client assumes us-east-1 and a bucket elsewhere fails, so set AWS_REGION or aws_region. Path-style https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/... and virtual-hosted https://<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/... URLs are treated as S3 rather than plain HTTP and take the same configuration, so stale credentials in the environment can be refused where an unsigned request would succeed; set aws_skip_signature for public data. An http:// endpoint (AWS_ENDPOINT, as for MinIO) is allowed without allow_http.

  • GCS: the GOOGLE_* variables (GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS); google_skip_signature for public buckets.

  • Azure: the AZURE_* variables (AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME, AZURE_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY, AZURE_STORAGE_SAS_KEY, ...); azure_skip_signature for public containers.

  • Plain HTTP(S): no authentication. store_opts accepts client keys such as timeout and connect_timeout.

  • GDAL paths /vsis3/bucket/key, /vsigs/bucket/key, /vsiaz/container/key and /vsicurl/<url> are read as the matching s3://, gs://, az:// or plain URL. Other /vsi paths, such as /vsizip/, are not supported.

Supported formats and CRSs

  • Tiled GeoTIFF and COG with ZSTD, Deflate, LZW, JPEG, PackBits or no compression. Strip-based TIFFs are not yet supported.

  • CRSs are resolved from an EPSG code, else WKT in a citation field (proj4wkt), else the GeoKey parameters, which covers custom projections written by GDAL without an EPSG code, such as a centred Lambert azimuthal equal-area. Reprojection uses pure-Rust proj4rs.

  • NoData: the dataset-wide TIFFTAG_GDAL_NODATA, compared safely for NaN. GeoTIFF does not store per-band NoData; reading bands from separate files with separate = TRUE gives each its own.

Performance

On a 12-band, 26-million-pixel Sentinel-2 COG, a5px is about 7 times faster end to end than gdal raster zonal-stats (including polygon preparation) and 11 times faster than a terra and dplyr pipeline.

Profiling

Set A5PX_PROFILE=1 to print stage timings (fetch, decode, projection, cell indexing, accumulation, merge) summed across workers.
